title: SAML connector compatibility scanner and zero‑touch onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a non-blocking compatibility scanner and zero-touch onboarding flow for SAML 2.0 connectors that validates IdP metadata, surfaces deterministic remediation steps, and produces a sanitized, deployable connector configuration. This ticket scopes the backend probe/validator, UX integration hooks, and audit/logging requirements for operator visibility. The goal is to reduce manual setup time and reduce onboarding failures caused by common metadata issues (missing ACS, unsupported bindings, certificate quirks, clock skew, invalid entityIDs).
acceptance_criteria: Scanner can fetch metadata from an uploaded XML blob, a metadata URL, or SAML metadata exchange (via manual paste or discovery URL).

Scanner performs the following checks and reports structured results: XML parse, schema (SAML2) conformance, entityID normalization, ACS endpoints and bindings, valid X.509 certificate chain and expiration, signing/encryption key presence, required NameID formats, SingleLogout endpoints, and clock skew tolerance heuristics.

Result payload includes: list of detected issues (severity), automated remediation suggestions (what to change on IdP or on connector), and a recommended connector config that can be previewed and accepted by an admin.
Non-blocking behavior: the probe runs asynchronously with progress notifications; connector creation can be completed in 'draft' state and finalized after a successful or acknowledged scan.
All probe attempts are logged to the audit log with actor, tenant, input source (URL/upload), and final verdict for compliance and incident investigations.

End-to-end test harness with at least 6 IdP sample metadata files: Okta (standard), ADFS with SHA1 fallback, AzureAD with multiple endpoints, OneLogin with multiple certificates, a misconfigured IdP missing ACS, and a federated metadata bundle with nested EntitiesDescriptor.
Metrics: probe_count, probe_failures, average_probe_latency, most_common_failure_reasons exported to Prometheus, and an alert for sudden spike in 'certificate_expired' failures.
implementation_notes: Run probes in a sandboxed background worker pool (separate from synchronous API workers) to limit correlation between customer load and long-running metadata fetches.
Use a canonical metadata sanitizer: normalize whitespace, sort Attributes/Endpoints deterministically, and strip unsupported extension nodes before generating connector config.
Leverage existing OpenSAML-compatible parser (java/python library depending on runtime) with a thin Redwood wrapper that emits stable diagnostics codes (e.g., M01 = malformed XML, C02 = missing ACS).
Cache probe results per-tenant+metadata-hash with TTL=24h to avoid repeated network fetches; expose manual 'reprobe' action in Console.
Design the probe to be idempotent and safe to run repeatedly; treat remote metadata fetches as untrusted input and enforce timeouts and size limits (e.g., 10s fetch timeout, 1MB max XML).
Certificates: verify expiry and signature algorithm (disallow RSA-512, flag RSA-1024 as warning), and accept ECDSA/RSASSA-PSS where supported by runtime.
Integrate probe outcomes into RBAC v2: only account admins and users with 'sso.manage' scope can run or finalize a zero-touch onboarding flow. All users with 'sso.view' scope can view scan results.
Audit logging: every metadata ingest, probe start/finish, outcome, and admin acceptance must emit an immutable log entry (tenant_id, actor, timestamp, probe_id, outcome_code).
UX integration: the Console will display a three-state connector: Draft (scan pending), Needs Attention (scan returned warnings/errors), Ready (scan success or admin accepted despite warnings).
technical_decisions: Perform remote metadata fetch as unauthenticated GET; support optional HTTP(S) basic auth header if admin supplies credentials in a secure form (store in KMS).
Adopt asynchronous probe model using job queue (Redis streams or internal task queue) to avoid request timeouts in the UI flow.
Use structured diagnostic codes for scan results so the Console and API can present consistent remediation steps across languages/SDKs.
Keep the validator implementation modular so we can swap the underlying SAML parsing library without changing API surfaced codes.
Expose an 'allowlist' for IdP entityIDs for enterprise customers who require explicit trust anchors; default to automated trust but provide manual override in Private deployments.
tasks: Backend: implement probe worker and metadata fetcher (Diego) - create job type, implement timeouts and size limits.
Backend: implement parser wrapper and diagnostic code mapping (Sana) - integrate OpenSAML binding and produce stable codes.
Backend: implement result caching and reprobe endpoint (Diego) - store results by metadata-hash+tenant.
Console: draft UX for zero-touch flow and three-state connector UI (Lucia Park) - include preview of recommended connector config.
Security: define audit log schema and retention (Priya Kapoor) - ensure immutable append-only logs to existing audit pipeline.
QA: assemble 6 sample IdP metadata files and automated tests for each common failure class (Marco) - tests cover parsing and connector generation.
Docs: write admin-facing playbook and remediation guidance for common errors (Ava Chen) - include suggested IdP fixes and sample emails to IdP admins.
SRE: add Prometheus metrics and alert on failure spike (Jordan) - instrument probe latency and error histogram.
risks: Remote metadata fetch may trigger excessive network load or reachability issues for some IdPs; mitigating with retries/backoff, per-tenant quotas, and opt-out for manual upload only.
False positives on certificate algorithm compatibility could block valid setups if runtime supports broader algorithms than our validator; will flag as warnings initially and tune after rollout.
Storage of optional fetch credentials requires careful KMS integration to avoid leaking secrets; will follow existing KMS patterns and require security review.
